board will decide whether to approve a package of incentives that include a $23 million performance-based incentive and a $50 million construction financing program for Amazon.com. The incentives would be in addition to the $23 million Amazon would pay the county in rent over 15 years, which has already been approved by the board.
The Amazon deliberations come three months after the Arlington County Board approved a $600 million incentive package, which would be the largest in the history of the county, to lure the company to Crystal City.
Amazon announced in September that it would build its second headquarters in Arlington, and requested proposals from local governments across North America to host the new headquarters. Arlington officials have said the incentive package would be the largest in the country.
The Arlington County Board could make its decision Saturday afternoon or wait until Wednesday, according to board member Jay Fisette. No decision has been made on when the vote will take place.
More than 300 people spoke at a public hearing on the incentives

most people know the story of former NFL player Ray Rice.
Rice and his wife Janay had a few too many drinks, got into an argument, and then Janay lost her temper and hit him.
He then hit her again, and then dragged her out of the elevator and dragged her into the hallway.
After that, he tried to convince the security guard to let him go, and that's when the video went viral and the story came out.
The image of Janay Rice in a wedding dress, being dragged by her hair out of the elevator by her husband was too much for the NFL to ignore.
Rice was released from the Baltimore Ravens, suspended indefinitely, and now he's looking at a year or more in prison.
He's even lost endorsement deals.
Now I don't want to give the impression that I think Rice's actions are excusable.
They are inexcusable.
I have no patience for people who hit women.

HotSpot @ Home (WiFi) — You connect your phone to the HotSpot @Home network, making calls and accessing the internet over Wi-Fi. You'll still use your phone's cellular connection for calls while on the move.

HotSpot @ Home (Mobile) — If the network is on the move, you need the mobile connection for calls while on the move.

10-foot high block walls with exposed rebar sit behind a chain link fence as an ugly reminder of how quickly the oceanfront condominium market crashed here in 2008.
The beachfront condos that were once known for their proximity to the water, spacious interiors and luxurious amenities have become run-down eyesores with many units abandoned.
"It was a disaster," said Jayme Jones, who has lived in a condominium overlooking the Atlantic for about 10 years.
Since 2008, eight of the former condos have been demolished. The others are being taken down in stages.
The first two former condominiums to be removed include two buildings adjacent to each other at 518 and 612 New Smyrna Beach Avenue, which were demolished in 2010.
The demolition of the buildings on the west side of New Smyrna Avenue was completed in November 2010. The other four condo buildings that were demolished in phases started with the building at 518 New Smyrna Avenue in 2012

force yourself to focus on the task at hand during a run. Here are some tips to help.

Tip 1:

Start your run with a purpose. Give yourself a destination and stick to it even if you have to follow the path through a park or through the woods. Your goal should be to make it to your destination. If you feel you don't have enough time, focus on how far you've already gone. If you've only gone a block, that's okay, just keep going.

Tip 2:

Focus on your breathing. Focus on each inhale and exhale. Make sure you don't hold your breath and that you exhale on your downswing. When you exhale, try to push the air out as far as you can. You don't have to be a breathing ninja; just make sure that you are exhaling completely, fully, and completely.

Tip 3:

Consider music or other sounds to be distracting

They have managed to stop the authorities from razing the whole complex, but are now engaged in a long legal battle with the city hall over whether they can continue using part of the building.

follow a paleo diet because it helps you lose body fat and be leaner.
If you're not familiar with the food pyramid, the pyramid represents the recommended daily intake of nutrients that our bodies need to function properly.
The pyramid has an outer layer that's mostly carbs, and an inner layer that's mostly fats.
The paleo diet falls under the protein-rich foods category.
Paleo dishes tend to be leaner and lower in carbs than conventional foods, and the theory is that eating paleo dishes helps your body get the nutrition it needs to grow strong and healthy.
The diet is essentially what our ancestors ate before we started eating foods that came with modern agriculture.
In theory, a paleo diet helps your body adapt to the foods you're eating by making you produce healthy hormones.
But there have been some problems with the paleo diet, and many people find it difficult to follow.

original:
Li, Steven Weber, and Mark G. Thompson.
Since China now produces more scientific research than the United States, many people assume that the country is on the cusp of becoming an innovation powerhouse. Yet the latest data on Chinese innovation suggest that this is unlikely.
China’s research spending is indeed growing, but it’s growing more slowly than in other nations, and the growth in the number of Chinese scientists is not keeping pace with the growing number of their peers around the world.
Moreover, more Chinese researchers are getting government funding to do science than those in the United States or Europe. But China invests its government money more inefficiently, and its scientists are more likely to work in “backward and obsolete” science than scientists in other countries.
The picture gets even bleaker when you consider how much government money China is spending on the military and how China is trying to export its technology, rather than the more innovative ideas generated in its universities.

corporate executives’ stock awards.

The vote is an initial step in implementing the Dodd-Frank Act, which the Obama administration passed in the wake of the financial crisis.
The requirements for executive pay, which must be approved by the agency’s commissioners, would apply to companies that have at least $1 billion in market value.

I've made it in a square pan, a loaf pan, in a casserole dish, etc. It's one of my favorite Thanksgiving desserts. Here's a delicious recipe that I make all year long.

Sweet Potato Casserole

Adapted from a recipe from Better Homes and Gardens, in the October/November 1997 issue

Preheat oven to 350 degrees.

Melt butter in large saucepan over medium heat. Add onions and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in flour and cook, stirring, until golden, about 5 minutes. Add milk, salt, and pepper to taste. Cook and stir until thickened, about 5 minutes. Stir in sweet potatoes and remove from heat. Spread into prepared pan. Place in the oven
